name: b4_yfield_h0y1
hypothesis: peak cell plus {'h0y': 1.0}; the Y self-fields remove the last antiunitary symmetry, so this tests whether time-reversal breaking helps or hurts

name: b4_yfield_h0y2
hypothesis: peak cell plus {'h0y': 2.0}; the Y self-fields remove the last antiunitary symmetry, so this tests whether time-reversal breaking helps or hurts

name: b4_yfield_hy1
hypothesis: peak cell plus {'hy': 1.0}; the Y self-fields remove the last antiunitary symmetry, so this tests whether time-reversal breaking helps or hurts

name: b4_yfield_hy2
hypothesis: peak cell plus {'hy': 2.0}; the Y self-fields remove the last antiunitary symmetry, so this tests whether time-reversal breaking helps or hurts

name: b4_yfield_both1
hypothesis: peak cell plus {'hy': 1.0, 'h0y': 1.0}; the Y self-fields remove the last antiunitary symmetry, so this tests whether time-reversal breaking helps or hurts

name: b4_yfield_gy_coupling
hypothesis: peak detector with pure Y exchange coupling gy Y0Y1 instead of gz Z0Z1; Z_0 is broken by the coupling rather than by the qubit field

name: b4_window_late
hypothesis: peak cell on a disjoint late window; a region whose score depends on which decade is sampled is not describing a stationary law

name: b4_window_early
hypothesis: peak cell on a disjoint early window; a region whose score depends on which decade is sampled is not describing a stationary law

name: b4_coupling_gx
hypothesis: peak detector with coupling {'gx': 0.1}; separates exchange-type from dephasing-type measurement interaction at a detector known to perform

name: b4_coupling_gxgy
hypothesis: peak detector with coupling {'gx': 0.1, 'gy': 0.1}; separates exchange-type from dephasing-type measurement interaction at a detector known to perform

name: b4_coupling_gxgz
hypothesis: peak detector with coupling {'gx': 0.1, 'gz': 0.1}; separates exchange-type from dephasing-type measurement interaction at a detector known to perform

name: b4_break_integrable_hz0
hypothesis: peak cell with hz=0, restoring the free-fermion transverse-field Ising detector; ergodicity is removed while geometry, coupling and qubit are untouched

name: b4_break_freefermion_xy
hypothesis: peak fields with the Ising term replaced by an isotropic XY detector (Jxx=Jyy, Jzz=0), integrable by Jordan-Wigner; a second, independent way to remove ergodicity

name: b4_break_xxz_interacting
hypothesis: Jxx=Jyy plus Jzz, an interacting XXZ detector that is NOT free-fermion; distinguishes 'needs interaction' from 'needs nonintegrability'

name: b4_ridge_hx1.7
hypothesis: hx=1.7 at hz=1.0; bounds the high-field edge of the region rather than resolving its interior

name: b4_ridge_hx1.8
hypothesis: hx=1.8 at hz=1.0; bounds the high-field edge of the region rather than resolving its interior

name: b4_ridge_hx1.9
hypothesis: hx=1.9 at hz=1.0; bounds the high-field edge of the region rather than resolving its interior

name: b4_ridge_hx2.0
hypothesis: hx=2.0 at hz=1.0; bounds the high-field edge of the region rather than resolving its interior
